findings.impact: The fill comparison may make learners infer that stuffing always foregrounds pushing an object into a space, although this block also teaches ordinary food and cushion filling.
findings.evidence: Snapshot line 327 says 「stuff は押し込む動作に焦点がある」 without limiting that contrast to the insertion use. The same block correctly includes food and padding at lines 266, 291–299. Oxford stuff verb senses 1 and 3 cover filling a container and adding a food filling, while sense 2 separately describes rapid/careless insertion: https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/stuff_2 . Oxford fill sense 1 supplies the broader making-full comparison: https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/fill_1 .
findings.action: Qualify this one comparison as the insertion use, or broaden it to 押し込む・詰め物をする動作. Keep the sound broad definition, existing examples and score; no block reorganization is required.

scope_notes: The 12-block organization is proportionate to the expanded lexical coverage. The first and third noun blocks openly identify their pedagogical overlap; the major action, state, character, skill, taxidermy, rejection and failure readings are now distinguishable. No further numbered block is demanded merely to reach a count.

Block 9 explicitly differentiates the obstruction verb from the directly related nasal state adjective in its title, definition and frames. This combination does not conceal the agent/state contrast; keeping it is defensible. It is also clearly separated from the failure meaning in block 12.

The selected mount comparison is supported for preparation of animal specimens for display. It does not assert that all mounting is taxidermy or that every occurrence of stuff is interchangeable with mount.

Marked expressions distinguish angry rejection from abandoning a plan. The British qualification for get stuffed and nonexclusive Australian indication for failure stuff up are defensible. Low-priority technical and vulgar readings have useful concise labels rather than forced large blocks.
The optional unified core can remain absent: the proposed article preserves the meanings and does not force all contemporary readings through an unexplained filling metaphor.

All 79 example/translation pairs were inspected. All 46 original English examples were independently confirmed present. Numeric frequencies were assessed as global-English per-selected-sense editorial bands, not measured corpus statistics; no arbitrary exact replacement score is requested.
